text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Engineering concern Stork talks with Royal Dutch Airlines/KLM about taking over carrier's maintenance operations. (p1)
- Stork reports better than expected 1996 results. (p3)
- Amsterdam stock and options exchange threatens to sue finance minister over report on demise of broker Nusse Brink. (p1)
- Retailer Ahold and Brazilian partner Bompreco take over shop chain SuperMar. (p1)
- Strong dollar pushes AEX to new high at 753.40. (p1)
- Window coverings maker Hunter Douglas upbeat about prospects. (p3)
- Retailer Vendex Int. sells five percent stake in Barnes & Noble. (p3)
- U.S. engineering group Chicago Bridge & Iron company to be listed on Amsterdam and New York stock exchanges at end of March. (p4)
VOLKSKRANT
- Saudi prince Al-Waleed bin Talal wants to take over bankrupt aircraft maker Fokker if asked. (p1)
- PM Wim Kok wards off parliamentary crisis over extension of NATO. (p1)
- Parliament supports newspaper publishers in price-fixing debate today. (p2)
- Stockbroker Van der Moolen gives staff options as a bonus instead of money. (p17)
DE TELEGRAAF
- Philips Electronics vice-president Jan Tollenaar leaves company for personal reasons. (p1)
- 68 cents of every shopping guilder is spent in supermarkets, according to central statistics bureau CBS. (p8)
- Technical services group GTI Holding talks about selling unit GTI Industrial Automation. (p21)
- Trading and technical investment group Landre & Glinderman books 43 pct higher 1996 net. (p23)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Stockbroker Van der Moolen targets growth on Wall Street. (p10)
- Buying and selling shares via the Internet grows fast. (p11)
TROUW
- Amsterdam Schiphol Airport beats London's Heathrow at freight transport. (p1)
- Telecom companies PTT Telecom, Enertel and Telfort ask traffic minister Annemarie Jorritsma for allowance on price fixing. (p7)
